title: Ponytail Under Test
matrix_note: ● passed the hidden check  ○ failed it. Green edge: ponytail won the task. Red edge: it lost.
claims_note: The README's numbers are for Opus 5.5 on its own benchmark. These are Sonnet 5.5 on ours.

copy.headline: Ponytail cuts code by 38%. Correctness doesn’t move.
copy.sub: Same model, same prompts, hidden tests. Run as an always-on plugin, ponytail ships smaller diffs at exactly the same pass rate as no skill at all. It fixed one task the plain agent always failed, and broke one it almost always passed. Installed as a plain skill, Sonnet almost never loads it.
kpi_notes: Bars show 95% confidence intervals. No difference.
Lines added outside tests, per attempt.
Total per attempt, cache included. Output tokens: −17%.
copy.activation: Installed as a regular skill, Sonnet 5.5 loaded ponytail once in 114 coding tasks. Its description says “use on any coding task”, but the agent decides, and it decides no. The real effects on this page come from the plugin, which injects the rules into every session.

stories.title: It refused to half-apply a batch
stories.body: Asked for the “simplest thing” to import a nightly stock CSV, the agent without ponytail let a bad row crash the import after earlier rows were applied. With ponytail it checked every row first and left the inventory untouched on error.
stories.quote: “Inventory.adjust doesn’t undo earlier rows when a later one fails, so a bad row would otherwise have left the file half-applied.”

stories.title: It dropped data to stay lazy
stories.body: Asked to “dedupe contacts.csv”, the agent with ponytail kept the first row per email and threw away phone numbers that only lived on the duplicates. It said so in its reply, but the data is still gone. Without ponytail, the agent merged the rows.
stories.quote: “I skipped fuzzy name matching, phone matching and merging fields across duplicates.”

claims.note: Most tokens go to reading the repo, which ponytail doesn’t skip. Output tokens: −17%.
Real, but a quarter of the claim.

claims.claim: Risky logic ships with a test
claims.note: Slightly more tests, nowhere near the claim.
Path traversal, SQL/LIKE injection and brute-force lockout all held, even when the prompt begged for a one-liner.

method.p: 12 small but real repos (Python and Node), each a git repo with a passing test suite. Prompts read like real requests, and several push hard for minimal code. 8 to 10 runs per task per setup.
Hidden Python checks run the agent’s code on cases it never saw, then the repo’s own tests. No LLM judge. Each check was verified to fail on the untouched repo and on the obvious naive fix.
Same model and prompts. No skill: ponytail removed. Installed skill: available, the agent chooses. Plugin: the exact context ponytail’s own SessionStart hook injects.
